txt: He looks you straight in the eye. "I hear you, officer," he agrees. "What kind of a sum are we talking about here?"
He nods at the empty lorry cabin behind his back. "No one would ever throw a good pair of *high quality plastic* sunglasses in the bushes, mister." His smile widens.
He nods. "In her lorry there, but... I don't know if it's her... Are we cool now? I think we're cool now."
He raises his arms in mock alarm. "Don't shoot, officer! Have we got an arrest here, or just a shakedown?"
He smiles brightly. "If you say so, officer. I don't worry too much about politics. I'm an entrepreneur, you know? Whatever's good for business is good for me."
You see a Samaran street vendor surrounded by a motley assemblage of goods. When he realizes you're looking at him his face breaks into a wide welcoming grin...
"*Everything's* cool. The goods are cool, the customers are cool, the place is cool -- and one more thing, officer..."
"*Now* we're getting somewhere," the street vendor nods. "If you'd only give me a good reason as well..."
"*Who* said that? It's the fat racist, right? I bet it's him. He has an agenda against me, because I'm an immigrant who works harder than he does. He's a hater."
"... you're *very* cool." He makes both hands into finger-pistols and fires a few finger-bullets into the air.
"...it's beautiful. Beautiful freedom!"
"A cop limping down the street, bleeding from the shoulder, face bruised, looking like hell... You know what that is?"
"A good starter pair, officer! And when you're ready to upgrade, come back and see me!"
"A man who knows his style," the street vendor nods. "Much respect."
"Ah, yes. Lots of cops are." The street vendor nods, dead-serious.
"Ah, yes. Money is very important." The street vendor nods, dead-serious.
"All natural materials, see?" The street vendor interrupts, guiding your hand over the fabric. "Real wool, 100% skin-friendly! And they're yours for only 2 reál!"
"All of them, I don't know. I told you all I know. Are we cool now? I really want us to be cool now."
"All of them. Even the ones who've left. I don't hang out with them, I don't remember who has tattoos."
"All right!" He snaps back to his act. "Very cool. Let's cap this off with a *purchase*. A pair of funky sunglasses, detective. You deserve it! And *I* deserve it too, don't you think?"
"Alright, this should help you get back on your feet." He takes a ten-note from a leather pouch.
"An investment?" He raises a brow, intrigued. "What kind of investment?"
"And they can be yours for a mere three reál. My regular customers have passed them all up because they've got no taste, but *you* found them..."
"And what?"
"Anything for you..." He smiles again.
"Are you sure? But they look so good on you!" The street vendor frowns. "You should think this through, officer."
"Astonishing quality! Unbelievable prices!"
"But officer, I don't have that kind of money. There's got to be a more modest investment."
"But officer, bribe you to do what?" The street vendor's expression is dead serious.
"But see, they are the pedestal for my sneakers. If I let go of the speakers, where will the sneakers go? I can't leave premium lifestyle sneakers on the *ground*..."
"Cool. That's *cool*." He nods and settles back into the pile of boxes.
"Crowd -- you know? The drug crowd."
"Damn, officer, you look like a mega-secret spy, very secret," the man nods eagerly. "They're practically made for you. I'll let you have them for... two reál and fifty cents!"
"Deals so good you just *can't* pass this up!"
"Doesn't matter," the street vendor replies. "All that matters is the box. Check it out, officer."
"Don't be shy, these are premium-class clothes! Good quality fabrics, best retro design! Save the economy with your style, officer!"
"Drugs?" For a moment he's unsure how to respond. "I don't go in for that, officer. Drugs ruin lives."
"Economical, but also trendy!" the street vendor shouts. "Look first-hand, buy second-hand. Keep the economy moving!"
"Everything is good here!"
"Everything's still cool here, officer," the street vendor assures you.
"Exactly! It's such a small part of my life. It's in the rear view mirror now. I'm climbing out of that hole -- with ingenuity."
"Fair point," he agrees, "You can't have a successful business without a loyal customer base. How much is your loyalty worth?"
"Good choice, officer! Mega-sporty. And it's only 4.50 for you, sir!"
"Good joke, officer! Here we don't have permits, just economic freedom. Take a look around..." He takes a deep breath.
"Good joke, officer, you're very funny, you know that?"
"Good move, officer. You won't find a deal like this anywhere."
"Good one, officer. You're a funny guy! Now what can I do for you?" He nods toward his shabby wares.
"Gotta prepare for springtime, right?" The street vendor seems pleased.
"Hah -- that! You drive a hard bargain, officer. I respect that." He nods. "Okay, what's it going to cost me? Be reasonable..."
"Happy shopping, officer! Everything's cool here!" He gives you a thumbs up.
"Haven't you heard, officer? We've got to be economically conscious. Recycle your cash, keep it in circulation! Don't buy new things! Buy eco!"
"Hey -- why not support *this* local entrepreneur? You can start by buying a pair of sexy pants. Or cool sunglasses... maybe some macaroni?"
"Hyper cool." He nods solemnly, then breathes out a sigh of pride surveying the city around him.
"I can see you've a taste for luxury, officer!" says the shopkeeper. "Can't keep your eyes off those sneakers?"
"I can't go extinct, officer! I've got kids to feed. Once an economy goes extinct, it messes up the whole eco-system. You got to think about the consequences!"
"I don't know. I told you... I don't know her name."
"I don't know... I'm not local. I don't know anything about that."
"I don't know... maybe? If she is, I haven't gone near her. I don't get *involved*, I told you."
"I guess it can't be any riskier than speculating in exotic derivatives... how much are we talking about here?"
"I let the goods do the talking."
"I only accept *legal* tender, officer." He lowers his voice. "Unless that's code for something?"
"I think that's fair." He settles back into the pile of boxes he's sitting on, making himself comfortable.
"I would, officer, gladly, but I don't have any cash on hand, you know?" He winks. "But maybe if you *buy* something first *then* I'll have some money you can shake me down for. Sound fair?"
"I'm an entrepreneur, officer!" He begins counting on his fingers. "I've got sources, buyers, suppliers, distributors, manufacturers, wholesalers... all extremely cool and aboveboard."
"I'm practically giving goods away here."
"I... officer," he nods. He is genuinely perplexed.
"If, on the other hand, you wanted to buy the *sneakers*, too, I could maybe throw in the speakers for a little extra -- 50 cents."
"In that case, I cannot accept that as payment, officer. I run everything above board here. Cash only."
"Is this really the economy we want to leave to our children?"
"It *is* -- *practically* free. Yours for five cents a piece! Rock that tuna -- why not some macaroni too?"
"It's a *she*, okay?" he whispers. "The other drivers call her the *lady driver*. You're better off staying away from her -- the way they talk about her..." He shakes his head. "She's no lady."
"It's very cool of you to ask again -- it's the third time now. How about you give *me* money and I give *you* cool pants and sneakers." He points to them.
"Look around, officer! You see all these premium goods, just sitting there, *not* getting bought? We've got to keep the flow of goods moving!"
"Look, officer. I'm just the retailer. You'd have to talk to my supplier if you got questions about the supply chain. That's how the game works."
"Look..." He looks around and lowers his voice. "There's bad people doing *bad* things here -- that's all I know. Please don't get me into this mess, I've spent fifteen years working my way up..."
"Me? It's a boring story, officer. Who cares about the past? I'm all business now -- all Revachol."
"My man, officer, *you* make all this possible! Without you, this climate would be extremely bad for business. You're part of the gossamer state!"
"My man, you know how the game is played! You and me, we should work together. What do you think -- shake things up?" He winks.
"No luck?" the street vendor says, visibly disappointed. "Why not take another look, officer? Keep supporting the economy!"
"No need for discounts at Siileng's, officer. Everything's already on sale." He nods towards the crates. "Anything you want, 50% off!"
"No problem here, officer. I get all this from one of my suppliers, an extremely reputable guy."
"No way, officer, these aren't for sale. They're bad speakers, low-fi socialist junk."
"No! I just said I work harder and he's an asshole. I'm..." He stops to think.
"No, don't pity them, officer! These are old Samaran garbage. Don't even look at them! Check out these super-cool FALN 'Ultras,' instead."
"No, no. It's very cool, officer. You're a cool cop for caring about those things. You should buy cool glasses too." He points to a pile of sunglasses.
"No, officer, you're a high-class policeman who accepts nothing less than the best! Lucky for you, I've got the best on sale!"

"No-no, apricots come from Siigay," the vendor explains. "My grandma used to grow them. But Siigay is a shithole, that's why I came to Revachol. Here's much better for an independent entrepreneur. Less *laws*."
"No-no, don't look at the speakers, officer! Look at the *sneakers*!" The man points to the footwear. "The *sneakers* are the stars here!"
"No. I just forgot. It's such a small part of my life. It's in the rear view mirror now. I'm climbing out of that hole -- with ingenuity."
"No. That's insane... It's the fat hater! He's been eyeing me for a week and he sent you here. Maybe *he's* the one, huh? Have you thought about that?"
"Nothing, I told you. I'm not a dumb guy -- I don't get involved with that crowd. "
"Of course, I'll come quietly." A sly wink. "But perhaps I could convince you to arrest some of my wares, officer? With your money, maybe?"
"Of course. Fire away!" He settles back into the pile of boxes he's sitting on, making himself comfortable.
"Officer, do I look like *I* have that kinda money? Be reasonable."
"Officer, do I look like a drug lord? I don't have that kinda money. Be reasonable here."
"Oh yes! You got style, you got *personal* style. You know what you like." He surveys his consumerist kingdom with an air of satisfaction.
"Oh! Oh no! It's very simple, actually. Siigay is a shithole. Not good for independent entrepreneurs like this one here. That's why I came to Revachol."
"Oh, he's a good guy. I think you'd get along. I'll let you know the next time he's around."
"Oh, okay." Siileng stops, his face suddenly serious. "But why, officer?"
"Oh, okay." The man stops, his face suddenly serious. "But why, officer?"
"Oh, that visor is perfect for you, officer. It'll definitely keep the sun out of your eyes while you're shooting criminals." The street vendor makes a bang-bang sound. "And all for a mere six reál."
"Oh, very interesting choice, officer, very *high-culture*..." For the first time the street vendor's voice trails off, as he watches you inspect the glasses.
"Oh," he exclaims, appearing to wipe a tear from his eye. "They're so beautiful I can hardly look at them."
"Oh... I like expeditions, and I like you. I can give you..." He counts in his head. "... 10 reál."
"Oh." The street vendor pauses. "Look man, I'm not into *politics*. I like everyone. Check out the box!"

"Okay, look..." He looks around and lowers his voice. "There's *bad* people here. Doing *bad* things. That's all I know. Please don't get into this mess. I've been Revachol for *fifteen* years, working my way up..."

"Okay, look..." The vendor looks around, then lowers his voice. "There's *bad* people doing *bad* things here -- that's all I know. Please don't get me into this mess, I've spent *fifteen* years working my way up..."
"Okay, maybe I'm a lorry driver too -- a little. But that's not the most important thing about me, that's my day job. This is my *dream*." He spreads his arms.
"Okay, officer, they're yours. For 50 cents."
"Okay, officer," he finally says, "I can't leave a man in need like that. How much do you need?"
"On the one hand, these speakers are socialist garbage. On the *other* hand, you *did* buy the sneakers, so I don't really need them anymore..."
"Only the coolest goods in Revachol. I've got sneakers, speakers, *extremely* comfy pants too. Try them on right here. No shame -- only freedom."

"Shush, please..." He looks around, then lowers his voice. "There's *bad* people doing *bad* things here -- that's all I know. Please don't get me into this mess, I've spent *fifteen* years working my way up..."
"Siigay, Apricot Suzerainty -- it's all the same to me, it's all cool. I'm interested in sales. Go ahead, let's make one." He gestures to the boxes. "Super high quality, friendly prices."
"So you did! Now put them on and look at them, officer! Make the people jealous of your premium lifestyle!"
"Sorry, detective." The man grins as if the entire incident is already forgotten.
"Sounds like a fair deal all around." He takes a ten-note from a leather pouch.
"Speaking of -- why not support an independent local entrepreneur? I send half my profits back to my grandma in Siigay."
"Speaking of, could I convince you to support an independent local entrepreneur right now?"
"Sporty *and* practical, officer! Good choice."
"Step right up, mister!"
"Super cool! Now the premium lifestyle is yours, officer."
"Sure, mister, very cool. Take a nice long look, I've got all sorts of things here."
"Tapes, you mean like music tapes? No, music is *out*! Don't listen to music. I sell extremely cool sunglasses if you want get your *mojo* going." He points at the shoddy box on the left.
"Tapes?" The notion sounds preposterous to him. "Tapes are *everywhere*! They're worthless, kids throw them in the trees -- there's one in the bushes, right behind this lorry."
"Ten reál is a bargain for that kind of investment! You got it, my man." He takes a ten-note from a leather pouch.
"That you are, officer," the street vendor says. "Stupid me! Go forth and live that premium lifestyle!"
"That's *even* cooler -- you investigating narcotics crimes like that. But --" he points to the goods. "I am not a lorry driver, I'm just a street vendor. I don't know anything about that."
"That's *so* cool -- you investigating the local drug trade like some cool Narc. But --" he points to the goods. "I am not a lorry driver, I'm just a street vendor. I don't know anything about that."
"That's *so* cool, officer. Speaking of, why not support an independent local entrepreneur by buying some pants and glasses?"
"That's cool. Especially after you already said you're into them. All the coolest detectives in the movies do drugs *and* are very conflicted about it. Still -- no drugs here." He smiles.
"That's cool. Especially after you said you *don't* like them. All the cool detectives do drugs without liking them. Sadly I don't have any drugs on sale here." He smiles.
"That's even cooler -- you investigating that and all. But --" he points to the goods. "I am not a lorry driver, I'm just a street vendor. I don't know anything about that."
"That's good, officer! That's exactly what the economy wants you to do."
"That's right, no permits, no bureaucracy! That's why this city -- *and* its law officials -- are *so* cool!"
"That's right, officer!" The street vendor flashes you a smile. "You're a high-class policeman who accepts nothing less than the best! Lucky for you, I've got the best on sale!"
"That's right, officer, but it's a bad scene for business there. Too many regulations, extremely bad for an independent local entrepreneur."

"That's right. Revachol is the best place for an independent self-employer like myself. That's why it's so *cool* with all the models coming here and cool celebrities..." He smiles his bright toothpaste-ad smile.
"That's the spirit! We've all got to do our part. Your part is to open the box and buy some clothes."
"That's very cool, a lot of the coolest detectives do drugs. Sadly, I don't have any drugs on sale -- or at my home. Or on my person." He smiles.
"That's very cool. I don't like drugs, either. I only said I do because I didn't want to sound *lame*." He smiles. "Peer pressure."
"The junk is yours, officer," the street vendor hands you the speakers. "Happy listening! Try not to hurt your ears with that Samaran garbage."
"The shine on these sunglasses lasts a lifetime, officer! One hundred percent guaranteed!"
"Then fire away, officer!" He settles back into the pile of boxes he's sitting on, getting comfortable.
"Then look at them again! These are premium lifestyle sneakers, officer -- the best on the market!"
"There's one by the statue of that king." He points towards the roundabout. "I haven't gone near her. And I *won't* either."
"There's something here for everyone!"

"These are all first-rate sunglasses!" the man declares. "Premium design, superb material, *very cool* UV-resistant! These will definitely keep your eyes safe *and* cool while doing your dangerous police work."
"These, officer? These speakers are Samaran garbage. I'm ashamed to even use them for props. Don't waste your time on them."
"They're *very* delicious. *And* shelf stable. You can keep all this out in the sun come summer! Try it -- buy some tuna. Won't rot. Un-rottable."
"Those sneakers, mister..." the street vendor intones. "Those sneakers are the latest FALN sneakers. Super-rare, super-fine, super-cool -- only 50 reál!"
"Too bad, officer. Kids make it all worthwhile. Without kids, who's going to be around to enjoy the economy?" He points at the clothes. "Don't let me stop you. Open the box and browse a little!"
"Unless *you're* into drugs, of course -- in which case, drugs are *excellent*." He kisses his fingers. "Tasty-tasty drugs."

"Very cool," Siileng nods, his eyebrows furrowed, "I admire your awareness of our intertwined histories. It's super nice of you to apologize for colonialism. But the Apricot Suzerainty is a shithole -- that's why I left."

"Very cool," the street vendor nods, his eyebrows furrowed, "I admire your awareness of our intertwined histories. It's super nice of you to apologize for colonialism. But the Apricot Suzerainty is a shithole -- that's why I left."
"Very cool. I like your style, officer."
"Very cool. The economy thanks you, officer."
"Very sharp, officer. I'm Seraise, from the Siigay province of the Seraise Empire. The 'Apricot Suzerainty', you know?"
"Well, if you *want* them..." He pauses for a moment, calculating.
"What, change your mind, officer?"
"What, no finger-pistols, officer?" The street vendor makes a little *pew-pew* sound.
"What, only a fiver? You can't even buy a pack of Royal Extras with that -- let's make this one *stick*, my friend!"
"What, only a fiver? You can't even buy a pack of Royal Extras with that -- let's make this one *stick*, my man."
"What? No. I can't believe you said that! You got *personal* style! You know what you like."
"What?" The street vendor looks over his left shoulder and stares at the lorry -- as though he's never seen a lorry in his entire life.
"Wow! So cool... you keep saying *the same sentence*, mister. No difference. Same words." He grins in amazement. "Let me donate you some sunglasses. For only 20 cents to 2 reál."
"Wow, officer, you look so cool," the street vendor has picked up his pace again, as you observe the world through deep sea-tinted lenses.
"Wow."

"Yeah -- *cool* ruins," he agrees. "I get to sell quality goods like these by cutting out the middlemen. *You* don't have to rebuild your house. Live in a crater! Or in a tree!" He points to a tree. "*Where* can you do that? Only here."
"Yeah, Revachol's the coolest. Doesn't care about where you're from, who you are... It's all about *freedom*." He nods admiringly.
"Yeah, that's the main thing about you." He nods admiringly. "Freedom is great, it's what lets independent entrepreneurs, like me, sell quality goods at competitive prices."

"Yes, apricots come from Siigay," the man explains. "My grandma used to grow them. But Siigay is a shithole, that's why I came to Revachol. Here's much better for an independent entrepreneur. Less *laws*."
"You do, officer, you do! Remember -- we don't have to resort to socialism, we can have nice things too! At socialist *prices*." He pats the boxes tenderly.
"You don't like it? Sure, square-jaw, no problem. Let's get you some real shades."
"You keep coming back. That's good, officer! Keep browsing those clothes, keep saving that economy!"
"You like premium menswear! Look around and browse, everything looks cool on a guy like you. Take your time." He settles back into the pile of boxes he's sitting on.
"You like sunglasses, officer? I've got the latest styles, right here!" The vendor takes a pair of sunglasses and sticks them under your nose.
"You mean these *delicious* pre-packaged, shelf-stable meal kits? Really easy to cook, no hassle, *really* cheap too -- buy some, try them out!"
"You see, I'm an honest entrepreneur. I can't help you if you don't give me a good reason as to why I should -- sorry, detective." The man grins as if the entire incident is already forgotten.
"You won't regret it, officer!" The street vendor smiles broadly.
"You're *guaranteed* to find something exciting!"
"You're right, officer, 100%." He returns his finger-pistols to their finger-holsters. "No playing around then. Strictly business. Maybe I can interest you in some premium menswear instead?"
"You're threatening my inviolable property rights?" He inhales dramatically, then simmers down.
